title: Animal Skeletons
seo_title: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: Animal Skeletons Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology: Animal skeletons; skeletons as structures
standard_text: Vertebrates have skeletons inside their bodies made of bones; the skeleton supports the body, protects organs and works with muscles for movement. Some animals have hard outer coverings. Skeletons are natural structures; frames and shells are designed structures. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences and Technology, Grade 5, Life and Living: Animal skeletons; skeletons as structures)

key_big: A skeleton supports, protects and helps the body move.
key_sub: Muscles pull on bones at joints.
body_html:
How to think about it

Vertebrates (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals) have a backbone and a skeleton inside the body. The skeleton holds the body up, protects soft organs (the skull protects the brain, the ribs protect the heart and lungs) and gives muscles something to pull on.

Joints such as the elbow and knee let the skeleton bend. Muscles work in pairs: one contracts to pull a bone, the other relaxes. Invertebrates such as insects and crabs have a hard outer covering instead. Skeletons are natural frame structures, like the frames of buildings.

Example

Which bones protect the heart and lungs?

They form a cage.

Answer: the ribs

Example

Does an earthworm have a skeleton of bones?

Is it a vertebrate?

Answer: no, it is an invertebrate

Common mistakes

  • Thinking muscles can push.
  • Thinking all animals have bones.
  • Thinking bones are not alive.
